metadata.source: MedDialog-EN (iCliniq + HealthCareMagic), mined offline, plus clinical follow-up questions
metadata.description: First questions and condition statistics learned from 212,098 real doctor-patient dialogs; follow-up questions (up to 10 layers in total) follow standard clinical history-taking; emergency red flags and advice are curated clinical guidance. This is an information tool, not a diagnosis.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Irregular periods with acne, extra facial hair, or weight gain can point to PCOS or another hormonal cause. Blood tests and an ultrasound help confirm it.

Your answers fit best with: Hormonal imbalance or PCOS.
homeCareInstructions: Ask your doctor about hormone and thyroid blood tests and a pelvic ultrasound
Regular exercise and a balanced diet help even if weight changes are small
Keep a calendar of your periods
indianHomeRemedies: Choose whole grains, dal, vegetables, and nuts, and cut down on maida, sugar, and cold drinks
Surya namaskar, brisk walking, or yoga for 30 minutes most days
Cumin (jeera) water in the morning is a common habit; check with your doctor before using methi, cinnamon, or turmeric in large amounts
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Book a visit if periods stop for 3 months, bleeding is very heavy, or you are trying to conceive.

periods_dx4.question: Assessment: Stress or weight-related cycle change

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Major stress, heavy exercise, dieting or weight loss can switch off ovulation temporarily and delay or stop periods. This is common and usually reversible.

Your answers fit best with: Stress or weight-related cycle change; Hormonal imbalance or PCOS; Thyroid disorder.
homeCareInstructions: Eat regular, sufficient meals and avoid crash dieting
Reduce very intense exercise if your periods have stopped
Aim for regular sleep and ways to manage stress
indianHomeRemedies: Regular sleep, yoga, and pranayama to lower stress
Eat regular meals with dal, greens, and seasonal fruit; avoid crash diets
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: See a doctor if you miss 3 periods in a row, you are trying to conceive, or you have symptoms such as hot flushes or bone pain.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
A late or missed period after sex can mean pregnancy. A home urine test is accurate from the first day of a missed period.

Your answers fit best with: Pregnancy; Stress or weight-related cycle change.
homeCareInstructions: Take a home pregnancy test; repeat in a few days if negative and the period has not come
If positive, book an early appointment and start folic acid
Avoid alcohol, smoking, and medicines that are unsafe in pregnancy
indianHomeRemedies: For morning nausea: dry snacks like roasted chana or khakhra before getting up, small frequent meals, and a little ginger or lemon
Avoid papaya (raw or unripe), large amounts of ajwain, and herbal kadhas unless your gynaecologist agrees
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Seek urgent care for severe one-sided belly pain, heavy bleeding, or fainting.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Major stress, heavy exercise, dieting or weight loss can switch off ovulation temporarily and delay or stop periods. This is common and usually reversible.

Your answers fit best with: Stress or weight-related cycle change; Fibroid or ovarian cyst; Pelvic or vaginal infection.
homeCareInstructions: Eat regular, sufficient meals and avoid crash dieting
Reduce very intense exercise if your periods have stopped
Aim for regular sleep and ways to manage stress
indianHomeRemedies: Regular sleep, yoga, and pranayama to lower stress
Eat regular meals with dal, greens, and seasonal fruit; avoid crash diets
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: See a doctor if you miss 3 periods in a row, you are trying to conceive, or you have symptoms such as hot flushes or bone pain.

conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now or go to the nearest emergency department.

numbness_em_stroke.question: Emergency: Possible stroke
numbness_em_stroke.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

likelyConditions: Other sudden brain or nerve emergency
conclusion.clinicalAdvice: Sudden weakness, face drooping, slurred speech, or loss of vision can mean a stroke. Treatment works best in the first hours, so do not wait to see if it passes.
homeCareInstructions: Note the exact time the symptoms began and tell the ambulance crew
Do not eat, drink, or take aspirin or other medicine unless a doctor tells you to
Lie down with your head slightly raised and stay with someone
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now. Do not drive yourself.

numbness_em_cauda.question: Emergency: Possible spinal nerve compression
numbness_em_cauda.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice: New numbness around the groin, loss of bladder or bowel control, or sudden leg weakness with back pain needs an urgent spinal scan. Delay can cause permanent damage.
homeCareInstructions: Do not wait to see if it improves
Avoid bending or lifting
Go to an emergency department now
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Go to the nearest emergency department now. Call 112 if you cannot walk.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes, with painful swelling in several joints, can mean inflammatory arthritis. Early treatment prevents joint damage.

Your answers fit best with: Rheumatoid or inflammatory arthritis.
homeCareInstructions: Ask for blood tests such as ESR, CRP, and rheumatoid factor
Gentle movement and a warm shower ease stiffness
Rest an acutely swollen joint but keep other joints moving
indianHomeRemedies: Warm compress or a warm bath for morning stiffness
Gentle yoga and joint movements in the morning
Haldi doodh is a comfort drink only; keep taking prescribed medicines
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Seek urgent care for a single hot, red, swollen joint with fever.

fatigue_d125.explanation:

Why we ask: A Yes points toward Insomnia or poor sleep or Depression.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice:
Passing a lot of urine, constant thirst, tiredness, tingling, or slow healing can come from raised blood sugar. A blood sugar test is quick and confirms it.

Your answers fit best with: Diabetes; Thyroid disorder; Sleep apnea.

Important: Tiredness with fever, night sweats or swollen glands should be checked promptly.
homeCareInstructions: Ask for a fasting blood sugar or HbA1c test
Cut back on sugary drinks and refined carbohydrates
Walk daily if you are able

conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now. Do not drive yourself.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice: Drooling, being unable to swallow saliva, a muffled voice, or noisy breathing can mean the throat is closing. This is an emergency.
homeCareInstructions: Sit upright and lean slightly forward
Do not force food, drink, or pills down
Go to an emergency department now
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now.

sorethroat_em_neck.question: Emergency: Possible meningitis or brain infection
sorethroat_em_neck.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice: Fever with a stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, or a rash that does not fade when pressed can mean meningitis or a blood infection. Hospital treatment is needed straight away.
homeCareInstructions: Do not wait for the rash to spread
Press a clear glass on the rash: if it does not fade, say so on the phone
Stay with someone and keep warm
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now or go to the nearest emergency department.

headache_em_thunderclap.question: Emergency: Possible bleeding in the brain
headache_em_thunderclap.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice: A headache that reaches full strength within seconds, or the worst headache of your life, needs emergency scanning.
homeCareInstructions: Rest in a quiet place and avoid straining
Do not drive yourself
Do not take extra pain medicine while waiting
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now.

headache_em_stroke.question: Emergency: Possible stroke
headache_em_stroke.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

likelyConditions: Other sudden brain or nerve emergency
conclusion.clinicalAdvice: Sudden weakness, face drooping, slurred speech, or loss of vision can mean a stroke. Treatment works best in the first hours, so do not wait to see if it passes.
homeCareInstructions: Note the exact time the symptoms began and tell the ambulance crew
Do not eat, drink, or take aspirin or other medicine unless a doctor tells you to
Lie down with your head slightly raised and stay with someone
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now. Do not drive yourself.

headache_em_neck.question: Emergency: Possible meningitis or brain infection
headache_em_neck.explanation: This warning sign comes from standard clinical triage guidance.

conclusion.clinicalAdvice: Fever with a stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, or a rash that does not fade when pressed can mean meningitis or a blood infection. Hospital treatment is needed straight away.
homeCareInstructions: Do not wait for the rash to spread
Press a clear glass on the rash: if it does not fade, say so on the phone
Stay with someone and keep warm
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now or go to the nearest emergency department.

headache_em_injury.question: Emergency: Possible serious head injury

Note vomiting, drowsiness, or any change in behaviour
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Call 112 now.

Persistent low mood, loss of interest, poor sleep, or tiredness are signs of depression. It is common and treatable with talking therapy, medicine, or both.

Your answers fit best with: Depression.
homeCareInstructions: Talk to someone you trust and do not isolate yourself
Keep a daily routine with light exercise, sunlight, and regular meals
Avoid alcohol, which makes mood worse
indianHomeRemedies: Get 15 to 20 minutes of morning sunlight and a daily walk, even a short one
Try yoga, pranayama, or meditation, and keep fixed times for meals and sleep
Talk to someone you trust; do not take herbal mood supplements such as ashwagandha or brahmi without asking your doctor
conclusion.whenToSeekImmediateHelp: Book a visit soon. If you ever think of ending your life, call 112 or Tele-MANAS (14416) immediately.
